detail:
The International OCD Foundation (IOCDF) presents research as central to its mission, stating that advancing understanding of OCD and related disorders is at the heart of what it does. The Foundation reports that since its inception in 1994 it has awarded 156 research grants totaling nearly $11.9 million in funding, alongside fostering a community of researchers and experts and maintaining a research study archive.

Findings the Foundation highlights from IOCDF-funded research include demonstrated effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and exposure and response prevention (ERP) for OCD and related disorders across age groups, including via telehealth, and links between OCD and differences in brain regions associated with cognition, emotion, memory, and motor movements, as well as neurotransmitters such as glutamate. For researchers, the Foundation describes a Research Grant Program and an annual Research Symposium, and it also reports disparities findings, including that African Americans experience OCD at rates similar to the general population while being less likely to receive treatments such as ERP or medications.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about obsessive-compulsive disorder research.
summary: The International OCD Foundation describes a research program that has awarded 156 grants totaling nearly $11.9 million since 1994, funding work on OCD treatment, brain differences, and disparities in care.

title: Obsessive-compulsive disorder: the research the IOCDF funds
